content: The treatment plan and analysis were prepared by Dick Menzies, Nicholas Winters, and Jonathon Campbell from McGill University. The primary research question focuses on whether a 6–9-month treatment regimen consisting of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL) improves outcomes in patients with extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) who are either treatment-intolerant or non-responsive to current regimens, compared to other WHO-recommended regimens. The population of interest includes patients with XDR-TB or MDR-TB who may have additional drug resistance patterns, cavitary disease on radiography, or prior treatment with second-line drugs. This population also includes individuals with or without HIV, adolescents aged 10–19 years (if data is available), and those with comorbidities such as diabetes, malnutrition, or mental disorders. The intervention being studied is the Nix-TB trial regimen, which includes bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid administered for 6–9 months. The comparator group consists of patients treated with WHO-recommended regimens, including bedaquiline and linezolid, but without pretomanid. The outcomes of interest include treatment success, bacteriological cure, adherence to treatment, treatment failure or relapse, survival, adverse reactions, and the acquisition of drug resistance. The Nix-TB trial was an open-label, phase 3 study conducted in South Africa between 2014 and 2019. It assessed the safety and efficacy of the BPaL regimen in patients aged 14 years or older with confirmed sputum culture-positive XDR-TB or treatment-intolerant/non-responsive MDR-TB. The trial lacked a comparison group, necessitating the use of an individual patient dataset (IPD) for comparative analysis. This dataset includes over 13,000 MDR-TB patients and more than 3,000 pre-XDR and XDR-TB patients from 55 centers across 40 countries. Patients treated after the approval of bedaquiline in 2013 will be matched to Nix-TB trial patients based on characteristics such as drug susceptibility testing (DST) results, drugs used, and other factors influencing treatment outcomes. The BPaL regimen in the Nix-TB trial consists of bedaquiline (400 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 200 mg three times per week), pretomanid (200 mg daily), and linezolid (1,200 mg daily) for 6–9 months. Patients were followed for up to 24 months post-treatment. Comparator regimens include combinations of bedaquiline, linezolid, and other anti-TB drugs, but none included pretomanid. The analysis will compare outcomes from treatment initiation to a specified duration, censoring events in comparator groups beyond this timeframe. The WHO currently recommends regimens for XDR-TB that involve at least five drugs during the intensive phase and four during the continuation phase, with treatment durations of 18–24 months. However, these regimens are associated with poor outcomes, including low treatment completion rates, high mortality, and frequent adverse events. The Nix-TB trial offers a shorter, all-oral regimen that may improve adherence and outcomes, but its efficacy and safety need to be compared to conventional regimens. Treatment outcomes will be analyzed using WHO 2005 definitions, which include successful treatment completion, bacteriological cure, treatment failure, relapse, death, and loss to follow-up. Adverse reactions and the acquisition of drug resistance cannot be analyzed using the IPD due to inconsistent data collection but were carefully measured in the Nix-TB trial. Outcomes from the Nix-TB trial will be verified and reclassified if necessary to align with WHO 2005 criteria. The analysis will also account for relapse during up to 18 months of post-treatment follow-up. Statistical analyses will include descriptive statistics and comparisons of treatment outcomes between the BPaL regimen and comparator regimens. The duration of treatment will be examined, particularly for patients with successful outcomes, and deviations from intended treatment durations will be considered. Patients who die, are lost to follow-up, or fail treatment will be analyzed separately to account for early treatment discontinuation.
